meta.title: Ondra Window
meta.description: Window specification and version guard: one definition for the title area height, the drag strip, the traffic-light position and centre, the three column widths and the five breakpoints, two branches (hidden title bar with system traffic lights, or fully hidden with drawn ones), and a check of the version whitelist in the shell-side patch. It does not create a window: the upstream repository exposes no window service key at all - the Electron shell is not here - so inventing one would only produce a dependency that is permanently undefined. It does not patch either, which is why the applied field of the plan is typed as the literal false: anyone trying to set it true fails to compile. The guard follows the disease the handbook names: a whitelist is not a minimum version but the exact set that was verified, and a patch whose version is not in that set simply does not take effect, because taking effect wrongly is far worse than not taking effect - a misplaced title bar, traffic lights on top of content, a drag strip over the buttons, and no error anywhere. The expected versions default to empty, since empty means nothing was declared verified, and judging that as a pass would turn silence into a signature. The self-consistency check reports three documentation-level conflicts as they are: the relationship between forty-eight and forty-four, the one-pixel difference between twenty-five and twenty-four, and the twelve pixels by which the three columns overflow their breakpoint. No decided value is silently corrected, and nothing is persisted: the service holds no handle, no timer and no file writer, so it can only ever read.
